what: MM-ROWS's design runs, before the commit, on the tree before it: prototypes of bcir_tensor.c made by a generator from four features (chunk: the k-blocked nest a chunk of 128 rows at a time, every column block of a chunk before the next; width: an AVX-512 edge block computing the vectors its columns reach; order: a pair or group job starting with the part whose tasks are the larger; and the pool's partition for the blocked contract: rowsN a task per 128-row range over every column from N rows, tasksN a task's columns as many whole blocks as leave the job N tasks), every one held bit for bit to the tree by bitcheck.c, then timed against it with ab_gemm.c (base, prototype and A/A in one process) and in the step with step_parts.py

bit_identity.note: out_base: the tree's own build (clang); oldproto: the first draft, whose partition read the call's depth -- a chain's calls of depth zero tiled apart from the chain -- the negative control; cand: chunk, width, rows1024; cand2: cand with order; tree_*: the slice as committed, before its commit

chunk_rules_1_thread_24_rounds.taken: chunks where A's panel is 2 MiB or more and K <= 1024: where the panel stays in L2 the chunks only pack the tiles again (the 9.84M decoder's 192 x 384 x 1024 weight adjoint x1.080 slower with chunks where K <= 1024)

step_parts_T2048.what: ../bwd-keep/step_parts.py, 8 rounds a run, kblock+exp+reduce, 4 threads: the tree (base) four runs, cand (chunk, width, rows1024) four, cand2 (cand with order) two -- not interleaved within a run, the runs alternated

separate_process_screens: the first screens timed each prototype in its own process (pool_bench.c, five rotated rounds of best-of-seven): on this host they moved by up to x1.6 between runs of one binary at 4 threads (the 9.84M decoder's 1024 x 1024 x 384 read x1.596 in one screen and x0.965 in the next), so every number below is from one process holding both units
